meta.source: census section 6.5 gloss-noun table, drafted 2026-09-02 by an opus agent; consumer contract implemented in src/mine.ts
meta.dimensionEncoding: Each dim is a 5-tuple in SI reading. Integers are plain numbers; exact rationals are [numerator, denominator] pairs, matching dimQ() in src/convention.ts (which accepts exactly this form) and the 5-tuple layout of dim() in src/unitsEngine.ts. Only the wavefunction entry currently uses a rational, but the Gaussian readings under gaussianDim use them throughout.

flags.dimensionless: dim is the zero vector; the quantity is a pure number in every system.
flags.conventionDependent: The SI and Gaussian readings differ. dim is the SI one; gaussianDim carries the CGS-Gaussian one (half-integer exponents throughout the charge sector).
flags.coordinateConventionDependent: The dimension depends on the coordinate convention (x⁰ = ct vs t in seconds; a(t₀) = 1 vs curvature-absorbed), not on the EM rationalization axis.
flags.dimensionDependsOnSpatialDimension: The dimension is a function of the spatial dimension d; dimByD carries the readings. Never emit without finding d in the text.
flags.ambiguous: One gloss, several live quantities with different dimensions. Emit at reduced confidence and require a disambiguator from the surrounding text.

nouns.note: The default reading of bare m and M in the GR registry. In hep prose a 'mass' is routinely quoted in GeV under hbar = c = 1; the SI dim here is the restored one.
'scale' alone is dangerously polysemous (energy scale, mass scale, length scale) — resolve only when the sentence says which.
Distinct entry from length because r is the single most common declared symbol; the GR registry reads bare r as a radial coordinate.
'period' resolves here; a spatial period is a wavelength, so a declaration reading 'the period of the lattice' must be routed to length instead.
Same dimension as angular frequency: the 2pi between them is a registry fork (census registry #10, the radian collapse), never a dimension check.
rad is dimensionless, so this is indistinguishable from frequency dimensionally — the discriminator is textual (omega vs nu), never dimensional.
'speed of light' resolves here; under c = 1 the mined dimension will disagree with the paper's in-system reading, which is the expected disagreement, not an error.
The GR registry reads kappa (surface gravity) as an acceleration, fixed by T_H = hbar*kappa/(2*pi*k_B*c).
Unremarkable; included because 'where F is the force' is a high-frequency declaration.
In hbar = c = 1 papers energy is the residual axis and everything else is quoted as a power of it; the SI reading is what a restoration must land on.
Dimensionally identical to energy and torque — a dimension check can never separate these three.
Shares its dimension with luminosity; the astro sense of 'luminosity' is the same quantity, but 'luminosity distance' and 'luminosity function' are not.
Under c = 1 momentum and mass and energy collapse to one axis; the mined SI dim is the restored one.
'spin' is a synonym only when it means the angular momentum itself; a dimensionless spin quantum number or a Kerr spin parameter a/M is a different quantity.
Same dimension as angular momentum and as hbar — the reason hbar = 1 makes action dimensionless.
Dimensionally identical to energy density, which is why an equation of state p = w*rho passes any dimension check with w dimensionless.

Bare 'density' is the single worst gloss in the corpus: mass, number, energy, charge and probability densities all answer to it. The engine's GR registry already flags rho as a registry CHOICE (an energy density differs by c²) — mined 'density' with no modifier should be emitted with low confidence, never silently.

Counts are dimensionless in the 5-basis (amount of substance is off-basis); a per-mole reading would need a sixth axis the census does not carry. 'column density' is often per area instead — check the sentence.
Sigma in accretion-disc prose. Sigma is also the Kerr metric function r² + a²cos²θ in the GR registry — a symbol clash the dimension check exists to catch.
Same dim as energy; the SI habit of writing N m rather than J is a display convention only.
The 'of' in the head noun is why the gloss grammar needs an explicit of-tail whitelist.
Bekenstein–Hawking S = A/4 makes horizon area a frequent declared symbol in G = c = hbar = 1 papers.
Mode volume carries the atomic-units 4pi ambiguity flagged in census §6.4 — the reading differs by 4pi between the two epsilon_0 conventions.
An area, but almost never quoted as one (barn, a_0², Mb). Under hbar = c = 1 it reads as an inverse squared energy.
Indistinguishable from pressure by dimension. Differs from mass density by exactly c², the census's canonical rho ambiguity.
Dimensionless by SI fiat (rad = 1). 'phase' is a synonym only for the argument of an exponential; an optical path phase in radians is the same thing.
Dimensionless (sr = 1). Hidden solid angles are exactly what makes Jy/beam and mag/arcsec² refuse-list items in census §7.
Kinematic viscosity shares this dimension exactly; that coincidence is the Schmidt number.
Bare 'viscosity' is ambiguous between dynamic (Pa s) and kinematic (m² s⁻¹); emit with low confidence unless the sentence disambiguates.
Dimensionless, but the census records a live fork in its DEFINITION (ΔL/L vs δL/L, §6.5b cue 3) that no dimension check can see.
Under k_B = 1 temperature IS an energy; the Theta axis vanishes. The mined SI dim is the restored one and will disagree with any k_B = 1 body — expected, not an error.
Dimensionless under k_B = 1 — the S = A/4 form only makes sense there. Same dim as heat capacity.
SPECIFIC heat capacity is per mass (J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ = [0,2,-2,-1,0]) and molar heat capacity is off-basis; the bare gloss is the extensive one, so a 'specific' modifier must change the emitted dim.

An ENERGY, not a potential in the electrostatic sense — the naming is a trap. Census round 4 left one chemical-potential identity claim unadjudicated; treat a per-particle-vs-per-mole reading as an open fork.
SI reading. Gaussian charge carries HALF-INTEGER exponents (M^1/2 L^3/2 T^-1) — this is the census's load-bearing example of why exponents must be exact rationals.
The SI base quantity. In every CGS system current is a derived half-integer quantity.
Bare 'potential' also means the Newtonian gravitational potential (m² s⁻²) and the interaction potential energy (J) — three different dimensions behind one word.
In Gaussian, E and B share one dimension — which is precisely why the c-rider on B exists (convention.ts EM_RIDERS).

This is B. Carries the c-rider in Gaussian and Heaviside–Lorentz (B_gauss = c × B_SI-quotient) — a rider, NOT a dimension change within a system. Magnetic atomic units are ambiguous by exactly alpha (census §6.4): 2.3505e5 T vs 1715.26 T.

H carries BOTH riders in Gaussian (the c-rider and the unrationalized 4pi). 1 Oe = (10³/4pi) A m⁻¹ for exactly that reason. Note the gloss 'magnetic field strength' is claimed by both B and H in the wild — a genuine collision.
Bare 'flux' is polysemous (magnetic flux, energy flux, particle flux, flux density). The flux quantum itself carries registry fork #11 (h/e vs h/2e).
In Gaussian, capacitance is a LENGTH (cm) — the cleanest demonstration that EM dimensions are convention-relative.
Gaussian resistance is s cm⁻¹. Pre-1948 papers mean the international ohm (1.00049) and the 1884 legal ohm is a distinct unit 0.25% off (census §7).
Gaussian inductance is s² cm⁻¹.
In Gaussian, conductivity is a FREQUENCY (s⁻¹) — a favourite plasma-physics tell.
Gaussian resistivity is a TIME (s).

Matches CONST_DIM.eps0. DIMENSIONLESS in Gaussian, which is what makes 4*pi*eps_0 = 1 a generator rather than a unit choice. Note 'dielectric constant' usually means the RELATIVE permittivity, which is dimensionless in every system.
Matches CONST_DIM.mu0. mu_0 = 1e-7 (rather than 4pi×1e-7) marks unrationalized MKS, whose riders put 4pi on D, H, eps and DIVIDE mu by 4pi (census §7).
Bare 'dipole moment' is ambiguous between the electric one (C m) and the magnetic one (A m²) — different dimensions, one gloss.
The emu/G-per-Oe decade interchange lives here; census keeps it as row material, not a rider.
Not to be confused with optical polarization (a state, dimensionless) or a polarization fraction.
Carries the c-rider only (not the 4pi) in Gaussian. The famous '4piM (kG)' ordinate is a PLOTTING fingerprint, not a rescaling of M (convention.ts, magnetism-emu).
The 4pi*j form with j in abA/cm² is the variant-Gaussian detector in census §7 — warn, never translate.
Surface charge density is per area, not per volume — the modifier changes the dim.
The GR registry notes bare lambda as a REGISTRY CHOICE — an affine parameter written lambda would differ.
Spectroscopic wavenumbers in cm⁻¹ are the same dimension; the 2pi (k = 2pi/lambda vs 1/lambda) is registry fork #10 again, invisible to a dimension check.
Dimensionless. The full Edlén/Ciddor air-index transform is refuse-listed in census §7 when T, p and humidity are unstated.
Radiometric intensity (W m⁻²) collides with the radiative-transfer specific intensity (W m⁻² sr⁻¹ Hz⁻¹) and with a dimensionless line intensity. Low confidence unless the sentence disambiguates.
The unambiguous name for what 'intensity' usually means.
A power. Note little-h: absolute magnitudes carry −5*log(h), a sign the census had to correct in two rows.

The astronomical reading (W m⁻² Hz⁻¹ = Jy). Collides head-on with 'magnetic flux density' (B, a tesla) and with a radiometric flux density (W m⁻²). Jy/beam is refuse-listed for its hidden solid angle.
Dimensionless; census §2.11 refuse-classes optical-depth self-similar variables as a nondimensionalization, not a unit system.

Dimensionless ONLY under the coordinate convention x⁰ = ct with all coordinates carrying length, which is what the engine's GR registry adopts so that indexed tensors have index-independent dimensions. Under a t-in-seconds convention, g_00 is not dimensionless.
A length. GM_sun/c³ = 4.9255 microseconds is the geometrized companion figure the census had to correct.
A velocity SQUARED, not an energy and not a voltage. This is the highest-value entry in the table for catching a bad 'potential' resolution.
An inverse time, despite always being quoted in km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹. The little-h convention hides inside the numeric value, never inside the dimension.

An inverse length squared in the geometrized reading the engine encodes. A paper writing Lambda as an energy density (J m⁻³) means the OTHER Lambda, differing by c⁴/(8*pi*G) — a live fork, not an error.
Dimensionless. The engine's GR registry reads bare z as a redshift but dz under a differential as a coordinate — a prefix-sensitive reading a flat extractor will get wrong.

Dimensionless under the a(t_0) = 1 normalization used almost everywhere; under the closed-FRW normalization where the curvature scale is absorbed, a carries LENGTH. Neither is wrong; the paper must say.
The engine reads kappa as an acceleration, a reading fixed by T_H = hbar*kappa/(2*pi*k_B*c); a kappa = 8*pi*G paper means an entirely different kappa (convention.ts classical-kappa).

DIMENSION DEPENDS ON THE SPATIAL DIMENSION d: a normalized single-particle wavefunction is L^(-d/2), so L^(-3/2) in 3D, L^(-1/2) in 1D, L^(-1) in 2D. A quantum-field psi in 4D has yet another dimension (mass^3/2 under hbar = c = 1). Never emit this without the d the paper works in — the half-integer exponent is exactly why the basis uses exact rationals.

Dimensionless for a marginal coupling in 4D (alpha, alpha_s, g). NOT dimensionless in general: the Fermi coupling G_F is mass^-2, a phi^3 coupling in 4D is a mass, and away from d = 4 every gauge coupling carries mass dimension (4−d)/2. Also note convention.ts REFUSES a dimensionless generator — a dimensionless coupling belongs to the N axis, never to the unit axes.
An ENERGY (Gamma = hbar/tau). Papers quote it in eV, MeV or in Hz; the Hz reading is the decay RATE, differing by hbar. 'linewidth' in laser prose usually means the rate.
Inverse time. Under hbar = 1 this is indistinguishable from a decay width, which is why both entries exist.
A time. Half-life and mean lifetime differ by ln 2 — a numeric fork, not a dimensional one.
A length. In cold-atom papers it is quoted in Bohr radii, which drags in the a_0 = 28.0028 Mb cross-section bridge from the census backlog.

tests.sentence: We model the inspiral in the post-Newtonian approximation, where $m_1$ and $m_2$ are the masses of the two component objects and $r$ is the orbital separation.
tests.note: Exercises the comma-list template alongside the workhorse in one sentence; 'orbital separation' resolves by dropping the leading modifier.

tests.sentence: Here $H_0$ is the present-day Hubble constant and $\Omega_m$ is the matter density in units of the critical density.
tests.caveat: surface-form trap: mined dim [1,-3,0,0,0] but the paper's Omega_m is dimensionless
tests.note: The second triple is a deliberate half-truth the consumer must catch: Omega_m is DIMENSIONLESS (a density ratio), but the sentence's surface form declares it as 'the matter density'. The trailing 'in units of the critical density' is the disambiguator, and it lives outside the gloss capture. Flagged so the dimension-check stage has a case where the mined dim is right about the words and wrong about the physics.

tests.sentence: The Zeeman term is evaluated with no factor of $1/c$, where $B$ is the magnetic field and $\mu$ is the magnetic moment of the defect.
tests.note: Both nouns are convention-dependent; the sentence itself carries the census §6.4 positive-SI fingerprint (a Zeeman term with no 1/c), so the SI reading is the licensed one here.

tests.sentence: Let $\Gamma$ be the total decay width of the resonance, so that $\tau = \hbar/\Gamma$ is the lifetime in the rest frame.
tests.note: Pairs the let-template with the expression-carrying template; the expression hbar/Gamma dimension-checks against 'lifetime' exactly (J s / J = s), which is the §6.5 stage-2 check succeeding.

tests.sentence: The response is governed by the electrical resistivity, denoted by $\rho$, at the base temperature.
tests.note: Exercises the reverse-order template. Worth noting that rho here collides with the engine's GR-registry reading (mass density) and with the fluid-dynamics reading; the Gaussian resistivity is a TIME, so a Gaussian-convention paper writing the same sentence means a different dimension again.

tests.sentence: The induced field satisfies Ampere's law, where $\mathbf{J}$ is the current density and $\sigma$ is the electrical conductivity of the plasma.
tests.caveat: symbol is emitted with its \mathbf wrapper intact
tests.note: Exercises the argument-taking macro branch of the symbol grammar. The emitted symbol keeps its wrapper (\mathbf{J}); stripping presentation macros is the consumer's job, and it must NOT strip \hat or \tilde the same way, because those carry the §6.5 cue-(iii) meaning 'dimensionless / normalized' and are excluded from the grammar for that reason.

tests.sentence: The phase velocity is $c/n$, where $n$ is the refractive index of the medium at the pump wavelength.
tests.note: A dimensionless noun that IS in the table, unlike the dimensionless ratio in t18 — the difference is that a refractive index is a named physical quantity with a registry entry, while a bare ratio is not.

tests.sentence: In the tables below, $\mu$ refers to the chemical potential of the electron gas, measured from the band edge.
tests.note: Chemical potential is an ENERGY despite the name; this is the single most valuable dimension correction in the thermodynamics block. Also exercises the refers-to verb and the 'measured' stopword as a gloss boundary.

tests.sentence: We adopt the convention of Ref. [4], where $\Sigma$ denotes the surface density of the disc at the inner radius.
tests.note: Sigma collides with the engine's GR-registry reading (the Kerr metric function r^2 + a^2 cos^2 theta, an AREA). Not flagged as a contradiction test because the hub differs — but a consumer running the GR registry over an accretion-disc paper would hit exactly this clash.

tests.sentence: Throughout, $\psi$ is the wavefunction of the relative coordinate, normalized over the three-dimensional volume.
tests.caveat: dimension is d-dependent; the emitted [0,[-3,2],0,0,0] is the 3D reading only
tests.note: The dimension emitted, L^(-3/2), is only correct because the sentence says three-dimensional. The noun entry carries dimensionDependsOnSpatialDimension and a dimByD map; a consumer that emits L^(-3/2) without finding d in the text is guessing.

tests.sentence: We inject signals at fixed $h$, with $h$ the gravitational-wave strain at the detector.
tests.note: Dimensionless, and the census records that the DEFINITION forks (Delta L / L vs delta L / L) with no dimensional signature — a case where a passed dimension check certifies nothing.

tests.sentence: The interaction is parameterized by $a_s$, where $a_s$ is the s-wave scattering length in units of the Bohr radius.
tests.note: Exercises the synonym path (s-wave scattering length) and lands on a length whose quoted unit (a_0) drags in a converter-graph entry from the census backlog.

tests.sentence: Sources are selected above a threshold in $S_\nu$, where $S_\nu$ is the flux density at 1.4 GHz.
tests.caveat: ambiguous noun; the per-frequency reading is licensed by context outside the capture
tests.note: 'flux density' is flagged ambiguous in the table: the astronomical Jy reading (W m^-2 Hz^-1) collides with magnetic flux density (T) and with a radiometric W m^-2. The '1.4 GHz' in the sentence is what licenses the Jy reading, and it sits outside the gloss capture.

tests.sentence: $I$ is the moment of inertia about the spin axis, and $\omega$ is the angular frequency of rotation.
tests.note: Exercises the of-tail whitelist in the gloss grammar (without it, the gloss truncates to the useless head 'moment').

tests.sentence: The mode volume is computed with $\varepsilon_0$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity in the rationalized convention.
tests.note: Permittivity is dimensionless in Gaussian, so the emitted SI vector is convention-dependent; the sentence's word 'rationalized' is the fingerprint that licenses it. Census §6.4 records that the electric analogue of the magnetic atomic-unit ambiguity is a factor sqrt(4pi) = 3.545 in lambda and 4pi in a mode volume.

tests.sentence: Table 2. Best-fit parameters for the three samples; columns give the annealing temperature, the extracted mobility, and the reduced chi-square of each fit.
tests.trap: This is census §6.5b's guard case rendered as prose. A table whose row or column labels are METHODS OR MATERIALS is a results table, not a normalization table, and reading it as cue (i) emits a false generator on a paper with an empty generator set. Mechanically it stays silent because no 'the <noun phrase>' here is followed by a symbol: 'the annealing temperature,' is followed by a comma, and 'the extracted mobility' by a comma — so even the appositive template, the loosest in the set, cannot fire.

tests.sentence: The self-energy is finite after regularization, where the integral runs over all momenta $k$ below the cutoff.
tests.trap: The canonical 'where' false positive. Two independent guards stop it: the workhorse needs a SYMBOL immediately after 'where' and finds the word 'the'; the appositive template would otherwise capture gloss 'integral runs over all momenta' with symbol 'k', but 'runs', 'over' and 'all' are stopwords, so no gloss can span them. Remove the stopword guard and this sentence produces a spurious length-dimension triple for k.

tests.sentence: The notation follows Ref. [12], where $E$ denotes the same quantity as in Eq. (3) of that work.
tests.trap: A citation sentence wearing the exact syntax of a declaration. It is blocked at the template level rather than at the noun table: 'same' is a stopword, so the gloss cannot start, and the match fails outright. A consumer that relaxes the stopword list must then rely on the noun lookup rejecting 'same quantity' — a weaker guard, since it emits a candidate that a fuzzy matcher might snap to 'quantity'.

tests.sentence: We define $\eta = n_b/n_\gamma$, the baryon-to-photon ratio, which is fixed by big-bang nucleosynthesis.
tests.trap: A dimensionless RATIO must not enter the unit-axis glossary at all. convention.ts throws on a dimensionless generator with exactly this instruction — route it to the N axis or the dimensionless-conventions registry (census §2.1, §2.5). Mechanically: the we-define template captures symbol eta and expression n_b/n_gamma but its gloss tail requires the literal 'as the', which is absent, so no gloss is attached and the reference pipeline emits nothing. The (symbol, expression) pair is still worth routing onward — to the dimensionless registry, not here.

tests.sentence: Following the notation of the survey papers, $m$ is the comoving separation between the two haloes, expressed in Mpc.

contradictsRegistry.expectedConsumerBehavior: The per-paper declaration WINS over the registry default — that is the entire point of §6.5 extraction — but the clash must be surfaced, not silently resolved, because a mis-parsed declaration and a genuine per-paper override are indistinguishable at this stage. Emit a conflict record carrying both readings.

tests.sentence: Here $T$ is the orbital period of the binary, and the mass ratio is held fixed at 0.8.

contradictsRegistry.expectedConsumerBehavior: Same rule as t20. This one is nastier because BOTH readings are ubiquitous for T and the two dimensions are on orthogonal axes (Theta vs T), so any downstream restoration solve will fail loudly rather than return a wrong number — the good failure mode. Under k_B = 1 the two readings partially merge, and the failure stops being loud.
